resources.string: Funnel exposes this local service to the public Internet, not just your Tailnet. Check the service authentication and content before continuing.
Local target (HTTP URL or localhost:port for TCP)
Enter a target and a port from 1–65535. Funnel supports HTTPS, TCP or TLS-terminated TCP on ports 443, 8443 or 10000 only; it does not support HTTP.
Read-only assistant: inventory, generate a merge fragment and explicitly test a selected peer. FoxyTail never edits another proxy app or module configuration.

Choose the actual filter mode of a compatible Mihomo core. Merge these entries into existing lists; do not replace the whole configuration or global DNS upstream. Keep this Tailnet suffix policy before broad rules and use a unique proxy name if FoxyTail-Tailnet already exists. Host routes cover only the current node addresses, not every subnet. TUN requires tailscale0; SOCKS uses the applied local listener. IPv6 still depends on the proxy core and device.
Use a TCP service port actually open on the selected peer. Optional resolver port is the third-party local DNS listener, not the FoxyTail DNS port. Leave blank to skip resolver tests.
DNS UDP, DNS TCP, optional resolver UDP/TCP and the selected TCP service are independent checks. A DNS pass does not prove TCP connectivity, all Tailnet access, or correct third-party rules.
Detect the current environment and choose the existing filter mode first.
The owned FoxyTail DNS listener is not ready. Fix its settings or reported conflict before generating a fragment or probing.

Whitelist semantics differ from blacklist. Automatic conversion is refused: do not paste a blacklist exclusion into whitelist mode. Review and change the third-party configuration yourself, then detect again.
The applied environment is invalid or changed. Discard the old result and detect again.
Detect a ready DNS environment, choose a peer and address, and enter a valid TCP port. The optional resolver port must be valid and different from FoxyTail DNS.
Recorded module counters, not a real-time speed test. UID totals describe the module accounting scope, not all app traffic. Switching hourly/daily reuses this snapshot without another root request.
Traffic by direction · Vertical axis: bytes
Gaps mean no recorded sample; zero means a recorded idle interval. Exact values and time labels follow the chart for accessibility.
Search and copy operate locally on the displayed source and line limit. Pause stops automatic reads; Refresh remains explicit. Automatic updates also respect the global auto-refresh setting.
Checks run only when requested. Results remain available until replaced by another successful run; they describe that run, not a continuous health guarantee.
Collect module configuration, runtime status, routing, DNS and diagnostic logs. Collection is a separate action from the itemized checks.
Anonymized sharing mode is the default. Review the archive before sharing; anonymization is not a guarantee that every application-specific detail is removed.
Local mode retains identifying network and device information. Keep it private. Saving or sharing this archive can expose sensitive diagnostics to the selected app or recipient.

Back up module configuration and hooks. Restore uses the validated archive digest and current configuration baseline. Import and export use the Android document picker; the app does not read arbitrary root paths.
Saved is not applied or verified healthy. Restore only replaces saved configuration. Review settings and explicitly apply/restart afterward; restored hooks are not executed by restore.
Backups may contain private configuration and hook contents. Share only with a trusted recipient.
